bio.appearance: About thirty, lean and quick, ink-black hair cropped short, sharp jaw, restless grey eyes. Charcoal layers with a dozen hidden pockets. A silver magpie-feather pin worn inside his collar, the last gift from his mother. A thin white scar across his left palm from a bad lock at age twelve. He/him.
bio.backstory: Raised on the rooftops of the Tangle, Kit could climb before he could read and pick a lock before he could sign his name. The Magpie taught him everything except how to do the last job. The night she went after the Meridian she said, 'Back before the bells, little jackdaw.' The bells rang. She never came home. In the six years since, Kit has made a name as a second-story artist, running jobs for Crane and asking every fence in the city the same question. Tonight a whisper brought him to the Night Market, where one of the auction lots is listed as 'The Magpie's Key.'
bio.bonds: His mother Marisol Corvell, 'the Magpie', the greatest thief Vessarine ever knew, who vanished six years ago. 'Uncle Val' Crane, her old fence, who kept Kit fed after she was gone.
bio.flaws: Can't walk away from a lock nobody has picked or a mark nobody has beaten. Trusts old friends far too easily.
bio.goals: Find out what happened to his mother. Beat the building that beat her.
bio.ideals: Freedom. Nothing beautiful and no one living should be locked away. Rob the powerful, never the desperate.
bio.personality: Cool under pressure, warm with friends, allergic to being told something can't be done. Plans three moves ahead and improvises the fourth. Hides worry behind a crooked grin and terrible jokes.

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.name: Book

inventory.name: The Marchwood tally-roll
inventory.source: loot: the oiled-leather tube strapped inside the tax wagon's tailboard

inventory.description: In Quist's careful hand (a little shakier on the left margins): a bill of sale for the assignment of Sir Gerold Ambry's debt of six thousand crowns from the Charter League to 'the Lord of Crowsfoot', with the price left blank; and a printed form of loan at one in ten a month, secured upon the borrower's land, with spaces for name, sum and seal.
inventory.name: Quist's papers

inventory.description: A heavy, long-shanked iron key on a fine steel chain, warm from a dead man's throat, its bow cast in the shape of the League's scales.
inventory.name: The factor's key

inventory.description: The Thornbury house's brass desk seal: the Charter League's scales above the word THORNBURY, on a turned walnut handle, with a stick of the League's green sealing wax. Any paper sealed with it looks like the League's own.
inventory.name: The League's seal
inventory.source: stolen: the factor's desk in the League counting room

inventory.description: A sheaf of a dozen printed League letter-of-credit blanks on heavy watermarked paper, the scales printed at the head, spaces for sum, bearer, house and the factor's hand. Unsigned and unsealed.
inventory.name: Blank League letters of credit
inventory.source: stolen: a locked drawer in the League counting room

inventory.description: A fat green-bound register: every League letter of credit drawn on the Thornbury house for five years, by number, sum, date and bearer, with the factor's notes. Your own seven thousand is entered on the last written page.
inventory.name: The League's register of letters

inventory.alias: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.description: Two chests' worth of papers held as surety, tied in labelled bundles: loans to the miller at Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant's landlord and a dozen Marchwood freeholders, each with the borrower's seal and the sum owed. Together they record a little over four thousand crowns owed to the League by men who live within thirty miles.
inventory.name: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.note: The last of the League's Marchwood bonds: the three Thornbury wool merchants (300 each) and the Plough and Pennant's landlord (250), all to be paid by Thornbury's council as the town's fine on Day 16. Settled already: the Aldersons and Oxbow Mill. With Hesketh's men: the twelve freeholders' bonds.

inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.
inventory.name: Sealed League packets

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached).
